class.name: NetwParticipant
class.brief_description: Live handle for one accepted session player.
class.description: A view over one peer's row in the session, holding nothing but the peer id: every member is read back through the session when it is asked for, so a participant is correct after a rehost, a scene rebuild or a respawn without anything re-issuing it. One peer has one participant, so [code]==[/code] answers "the same player". [member current_scene] tracks the peer's primary scene membership independently of any spawned player node, which is what lets a session seat a player before it has a body and keep the seat after the body is gone. [codeblock] var participant := api.peer_get_participant(peer_id) if participant.identity: greet(participant.username) participant.move_to(arena) [/codeblock] Minted by [method NetwMultiplayerCore.participant_ensure] and never by a caller: the session mints the row the first time a peer is asked about, so two reads of one peer answer the same object.

method.name: move_to
method.description: Moves this participant into the [NetwSceneHandle] [param dest] without touching any player node. The seat and both admission boundaries move together in [method NetwMultiplayerCore.participant_move_seat], so a participant is never seated in one scene while admitted to another. A move into the scene already held changes nothing, and a destination that resolves to no scene entity is refused. [b][br][br]Server Only.[/b]

members.member: The typed join arguments accepted for this peer. See [member ResolvedJoin.arg_values].

The [NetwSceneHandle] for this peer's primary scene membership, or [code]null[/code] outside every scene. A participant is admitted to one scene at a time, so this is a scalar even though the mechanism underneath it is not. The seat is held as the scene entity's identity rather than as a handle, so membership survives the container being rebuilt and never pins a freed node, and the handle read here is minted from that identity on demand. Assigning it records membership without admitting anyone. [method move_to] is the verb that moves the admission edge too, and it is what a caller wanting a participant to actually arrive uses. Answered as a [Variant] for the reason [member NetwEntity.scene] is: the handle is the kit's and the session may not name its type.

The validated auth identity for this peer, or [code]null[/code]. Present only when the session has an auth provider, and never part of the replicated roster, which is what [ResolvedJoin] is. Read through the reader installed by [method NetwMultiplayerCore.set_identity_reader], because auth buckets are keyed by a GDScript type and the session cannot name one.
Whether the accepted join was a debug join. See [member ResolvedJoin.is_debug].

The accepted join record for this peer, or [code]null[/code] before the join is accepted. Read through [method NetwMultiplayerCore.session_accepted_join] on every access rather than held, so a join enriched after the participant was minted is answered by the participant that already exists.
The peer this participant represents. The one piece of state it holds, because everything else is a read.
The accepted username for this peer, empty before the join is accepted. See [member ResolvedJoin.username].

signal.name: scene_changed
signal.description: Emitted when [member current_scene] changes, carrying the [NetwSceneHandle] left and the one arrived in, either of which may be [code]null[/code]. Emitted by the seat verbs themselves rather than by whoever called them, so a seat written by a move, by a release and by a session teardown all announce the same way. A silent write is the failure this closes: a seat that changed without announcing leaves every viewer showing the previous scene. The session republishes the local participant's edge as [signal NetwMultiplayer.local_scene_changed], rebinding it as the local row comes and goes, so a game that only cares about this peer listens there and never has to hold a participant to do it.
